terms.grammar: plural of bōs; dative and ablative bōbus or būbus
evidence: Liv. 1.7: inde cum āctae bovēs mūgīssent (Lewis & Short s.v. mūgiō)
terms.comment: The plural of bōs, ox or cow (see ox, cow). Cattle as livestock in general is pecus, pecoris n.; a single head of cattle, one beast of the herd, is pecus, pecudis f. (Lewis & Short; see livestock).

evidence: Varr. R. R. 2.1.13: būbulum pecus, horned cattle (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Collective: the herd or flock as a whole (Lewis & Short, opposing it to pecus, pecudis, a single head).

sources: Lewis & Short: bos
Lewis & Short: pecus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 288.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
